title: Why can your phone switch off in the cold with battery left?

cards.title: Your phone says 30%, then switches off.
cards.text: It's freezing, and the screen goes black anyway. But the battery isn't empty. The power is still inside it, just hard to get out.
cards.hook: So what slows it down inside?

cards.title: Cold makes the battery's insides move slowly
cards.text: A battery carries power as tiny charged particles, called ions, swimming through a liquid. Cold thickens the liquid, like honey. The ions crawl, so the battery can't push power out quickly.
cards.hook: So how does your phone tell what's left?

notes: Cold: the liquid thickens and they crawl

cards.title: A weak push makes your phone think it's empty
cards.text: Your phone can't see the charge left. It works it out partly from how hard the battery pushes. A cold battery pushes weakly, so the phone thinks it's nearly empty. When the push gets too weak to run on, it switches off.

notes: Below the line the phone cannot run

cards.title: Warm it up and the charge is back
cards.text: Nothing drained away. As the battery warms, the ions speed up again. A typical battery gives only about half its charge at freezer cold, and gives it all back at room temperature.
cards.takeaway: The battery wasn't empty. It was just too cold to hand over the power.

notes: A battery at freezer cold gives half

cards.note: Charging a phone while it is below freezing can damage the battery for good, so let a cold phone warm up before you plug it in.
